problems.censoring: An object is in the sample either way and its value is known only as an upper limit when it falls below a detection limit: row {value, censored, limit}. A detection has censored = false and value = the measurement; a non-detection has censored = true and value = its upper limit (the object's value is below it). Left censoring. 'limit' is the detection threshold that applied to the object, optional for the estimator and required for the independence check.
problems.truncation: An object is absent from the sample, uncounted, when its value falls outside the observable range at its own distance or epoch: row {x, u}. The object is in the sample only because x >= u, where u is the lower limit of observability that applied to it; every object with x < u is missing and nothing records how many. One-sided (lower) truncation; the upper boundary is not modelled.
problems.vmax: A flux-limited sample of objects with a known luminosity and a known distance: each object's accessible volume Vmax is the volume out to the distance at which it would fall to the flux limit, capped at the survey's edge.

km.name: Kaplan-Meier-type product-limit estimator for left-censored data (the flipped form)
km.definition: M = the largest value in the sample; y = M - value; a limit becomes a right-censored observation at y (its true y is larger), a detection an event. At each distinct y of an event, n = the number of rows with y_row >= y (a right-censored row at the same y stays at risk), d = the events at that y; S(y) = product over events <= y of (1 - d/n). The estimated distribution of the value puts mass S(y-) - S(y) at the value M - y. Ties: events are processed before censorings at the same y.
km.mean: The mean of y is the area under S up to tau, the largest observed y. If the largest y is an event (the smallest raw observation is a detection) the mass is complete: status 'complete', mean(value) = M - mean(y). If it is censored (the smallest raw observation is a limit), the mass S(tau) lies below the smallest raw observation: status 'bounded', tailMass = S(tau), and the value-mean lies between meanLow (that mass placed at a declared floor) and meanHigh (that mass placed at the smallest raw observation). mean is null when bounded. A declared floor is required to bound; without one the call is refused (unbounded-tail).
km.variance: Greenwood-type variance of the area under S: Var = sum over event times y_i of A_i^2 d_i / (n_i (n_i - d_i)), A_i = the integral of S from y_i to tau; a term with n_i = d_i has A_i = 0 and is zero. Interval: [meanLow - z se, meanHigh + z se] (equal bounds when complete), z the normal quantile of (1 + level) / 2.
km.independenceCheck: Needs 'limit' on every row. Group 1 = rows with limit <= the median of the limits, group 2 the rest; the two-sample log-rank test (Mantel-Haenszel, hypergeometric variance with the tie correction) on the flipped data, two-sided, z and p from the normal. The check FLAGS when p < alpha. A flag means the censoring depends on the value in the sense this test can see: the result then carries status 'dependent' and no interval is offered. Not run (labelled 'unchecked', result still returned, interval labelled unchecked) when a row lacks a limit, a group is empty, or a group has fewer than 5 detections. It does not and cannot prove independence.
km.domain: The censoring (the limit) independent of the value, the same limit mechanism for every object, the value measured exactly when detected, at least 5 detections. No claim for a truncated sample.
km.citedForm: Product-limit estimator of Kaplan and Meier; left censoring by the flip (Feigelson and Nelson's route to it in astronomy); the Greenwood form of the variance. The equations above are this gate's own statement of those forms, derived and written without a source in front of the author; their agreement with the printed forms is request X4 and NOT RUN.

cm.name: Lynden-Bell C-minus: the product-limit estimator for a lower-truncated sample
cm.definition: Rows (x_i, u_i) with u_i <= x_i. For the declared 'from' (the value above which the distribution is recovered) keep rows with x_i >= from. At each distinct x_i: n = the number of rows j with u_j <= x_i <= x_j (the associated set, the object itself included), d = the rows at that x; the conditional survival S_c(t) = product over x_i <= t of (1 - d/n) estimates P(X > t | X >= from); the mass at x_i is S_c(x_i-) - S_c(x_i). Identifiability needs the truncation limit's lower end to reach below the support of the part recovered; the estimator is therefore defined only above 'from' and says so.
cm.mean: E[X | X >= from] = sum of mass times x (equal to from + the integral of S_c from from to the largest x).
cm.variance: The same Greenwood-type sum with the associated-set sizes: Var = sum A_i^2 d_i / (n_i (n_i - d_i)), A_i = the integral of S_c from x_i to the largest x; a term with n_i = d_i has A_i = 0 and is zero. Interval as for km.
cm.domain: A known one-sided truncation boundary u_i for every row; the truncation independent of the value in the parent population (the parents are drawn independently of the boundary and then kept only if x >= u); at least 10 rows in the associated set at 'from' (minRisk). Refused otherwise.
cm.citedForm: Lynden-Bell's C-minus method (1971) and the left-truncated product-limit estimator of Woodroofe and of Tsai, Jewell and Wang; stated here from the definitions, their agreement with the printed form is request X4 and NOT RUN.

vmax.name: V/Vmax and the 1/Vmax space density with an effective volume
vmax.definition: Vmax_i = V(min(dmax_i, D)), V the volume function (Euclidean 4 pi d^3 / 3 by default; 'unit' d^3 for the hand cases), D the survey edge. The statistic <V/Vmax> = mean of V(d_i) / Vmax_i; for a complete sample of a population uniform in volume V/Vmax is uniform on (0, 1): mean 1/2, variance 1/12, so z = (<V/Vmax> - 1/2) sqrt(12 N) is standard normal. With a completeness p(d) (a probability of inclusion at distance d for the object's luminosity), Veff_i = the integral of p(d) dV(d) from 0 to D, and the space density of a luminosity bin is rho = sum of 1 / Veff_i over the objects in the bin, with the Poisson-process variance sum of 1 / Veff_i^2.
vmax.domain: A hard cut or a stated completeness curve; a population uniform in volume is the null of z and nothing else; at least 5 objects; a luminosity bin with no object yields an upper limit, not a number.
vmax.citedForm: Schmidt's V/Vmax and the 1/Vmax estimator; the properties above are exact consequences of the definition; their agreement with the printed forms is request X4 and NOT RUN.

scenarios.population: Censoring population: X ~ Gamma(shape 2, scale 1), mean 2, floor 0 (declared). Truncation population: x ~ Normal(0, 1) with distance d from the density proportional to d^2 on (0, 1] and u = 0.5 + 2 log10(d), kept when x >= u; parents are drawn until N observed rows are kept. V/Vmax population: points uniform in volume in a sphere of radius D = 1 (Poisson, intensity lambda = 60 per unit volume), luminosity L = 10^(0.5 Z) with Z ~ N(0, 1), detection distance dmax = 0.8 sqrt(L) (a hard cut at dmax or, for the ramp, p(d) = 1 / (1 + (d / dmax)^8)).

censoringK.rule: T = max(X, C); a detection when X >= C (value X, limit C) else a limit (value C, censored). Replicate r uses seed baseSeed + r. The true mean is 2.

D1.rule: Za, Zb, Zn independent standard normals; X = -ln(Phi(Za)) - ln(Phi(Zb)) (so X ~ Gamma(2, 1)); Zc = rho (Za + Zb) / sqrt(2) + sqrt(1 - rho^2) Zn; C = 2.5 Phi(Zc). The censoring threshold depends on the value.

D1b.rule: as D1 with rho = 0.5; reported only

D2.rule: K2's marginals, independent (C ~ Uniform(0, 2.5)), n = 200: the false-alarm rate of the independence check

T3.note: reported only: the associated set at 'from' is expected to be refused or thin

truncationT.truth: E[X | X >= from] for Normal(0, 1) = phi(from) / (1 - Phi(from))

V1.null: uniform in volume, hard cut: z of <V/Vmax> over N detected objects, 5 percent two-sided rejection rate

V1n.evolution: number density proportional to d^2 times d^2 (so the points are denser outward), hard cut: the rejection rate of the null

C4b.completeness: ramp p(d) = 1 / (1 + (d / dmax)^8), each object kept with that probability

Measurement definitions the legs left open, fixed before any validator run: (1) L1's sup distance is the largest, over the support points v, of |c - F(v)| for c the cumulative mass just before and just after v, and the same with the tail mass added; |mean - 2| uses the midpoint of meanLow and meanHigh when the status is bounded. L2's sup distance is the same on the conditional CDF. (2) In every coverage and rate ensemble a replicate the estimator refuses (for example too few detections) counts as not covering, not flagged and not rejecting, and the number of refused replicates is reported. (3) The oracle's own ensembles (C1o, C2o) count a replicate with fewer than 5 detections or an associated set under 10 as refused in the same way. (4) The V/Vmax ensembles draw the number of parents from a Poisson distribution of mean lambda times the volume of the sphere (Knuth's multiplication method), the distance of a uniform population as U^(1/3) and of the evolving population as U^(1/5), and the completeness check of leg D6 samples the curve at 64 evenly spaced distances. No bound is moved.
The oracle's pinned output is run again against the thresholds file that carries AM1 to AM3 (the numbers are unchanged; only the recorded sha256 differs), so that leg I1 compares like with like.

decisions.text: The estimators are stated here from their definitions and checked against an independent implementation, not transcribed from a source: no text of the cited papers was available, so their printed forms are request X4 and the correspondence is NOT RUN. A verdict is therefore 'V-internal, synthetic and oracle'.

A left-censored sample whose smallest observation is a limit has probability mass below it that the data cannot place. The estimator reports bounds from a declared floor and no point mean, rather than the convention that treats the smallest limit as a detection (a labelled convention could be added later as a new leg).

The independence check is a two-sample log-rank test between the lower and the upper half of the detection limits. It looks for the dependence of the value on the limit; it cannot see every dependence, and the result says so ('does not prove independence').

The truncation estimator is defined above a declared 'from' and refuses a thin associated set there: below the point where the truncation reaches, the data say nothing about the distribution, and the Lynden-Bell estimator's early terms are unstable.
V/Vmax with an effective volume is tested here as a third group so that Part B does not extend tested scope; it does not enter the A, B, C letter.
